newsitem.title: USA: Boston subway overspent, watchdog says - report.
newsitem.headline: Boston subway overspent, watchdog says - report.

text.p: Boston subway system (MBTA) spent at least $26 million more than reported in in the 1996 budget and officials hid the extra costs, a watchdog group alledged, the Boston Herald reported Tuesday.
The Finance Committee of MBTA Advisory Board recommended that the full board reject an MBTA budget transfer request at a Thursday meeting, the Herald repoted.
The committee has also asked for an independent review of the MBTA.

"The Finance Committee would argue that had the T held to its bottom line, the cost to the state would have been $10.5 million less in the long haul," said Advisory Board Executive Director Annne Larner.
MBTA officials called the Advisory Board report "grossly inaccurate," the newspaper reported.
"We don't believe we misled anybody," MBTA Budget Director Jonathan Davis said.

If the MBTA had recorded a reserve drawdown of $15.4 milllion and $10.5 million earned in equipment sale leaseback agreements on its balance sheet , the MBTA's total operating expense would have been $516 million instead of $494 million., the Fiance Committee said in a report.
Davis said all of the MBTA's accounting practices were "appropriate."
